newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer, eying more Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer, eying more Greenspan.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer on Wednesday as investors breathed a sigh of relief after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivered upbeat remarks yesterday on the U.S. economy and markets.

One money markets trader said treasuries prices had slipped at the open from overnight strength as investors took profits following Tuesday's rally. "However, the tone remains positive," he added. Greenspan is scheduled to wrap up his Congress testimony on Wednesday.
Canada's three-month cash T-bill traded to yield 3.34 percent from 3.35 percent at Tuesday's close.
Traders said that investors were not as nervous about today's commentary although one added that Greenspan could deliver a less bullish message today to neutralize yesterday's market reaction.
Canada's money market was quiet on Wednesday after volatility earlier this week, one trader said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.64 percent from 3.65 percent on Tuesday. The one-year when-issued T-bill eased to yield 4.12 percent from 4.16 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.20 percent, near the middle of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
